'''Mei-Yin Chou''' ({{lang-zh|t=周美吟|p=Zhōu Měiyín}}; born 1958) is a Taiwanese physicist who was vice president of [[Academia Sinica]] from 2016 to 2026. She is a specialist in [[condensed matter physics]] and [[solid-state physics]].

== Education ==
Chou graduated from [[National Taiwan University]] with a [[Bachelor of Science]] (B.S.) in physics in 1980. She then completed advanced studies in the United States at the [[University of California, Berkeley]], where she earned her [[Master of Science]] (M.S.) in physics in 1983 and her [[Ph.D.]] in physics in 1986.<ref>{{cite news |title=Mei-Yin Chou |url=https://www.physics.gatech.edu/user/mei-yin-chou |accessdate=7 January 2019 |publisher=Georgia Institute of Technology}}</ref> Her doctoral dissertation, completed under physics professor [[Marvin L. Cohen]], was titled, "Electrons in Solids and Clusters".<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Electrons in solids and clusters |url=https://www.proquest.com/openview/6584411d1da5441b2625f8509a04939f/1?cbl=18750&diss=y&pq-origsite=gscholar |access-date=2025-05-08 |website= |language=en|publisher=[[Proquest]]|type=PhD Thesis|date=1986}}</ref> She published 12 academic papers before she completed her doctorate at Berkeley.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=Academia Sinica Vice President Chou Mei-yin: Set rules from a young age and encourage children to become independent early. |url=https://futureparenting.cwgv.com.tw/family/content/index/2806 |access-date=2026-03-04 |website=[[CommonWealth Magazine (Taiwan)|CommonWealth Magazine]]|date=2016-03-01|last=Lin|first=Zhian|language=zh-tw}}</ref>

== Acadenic career ==
After receiving her doctorate, Chou completed [[postdoctoral research]] with [[Exxon]], and joined the [[Georgia Institute of Technology]] faculty in 1989.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Goettling |first1=Gary |date=1991 |title=A rising star in physics |url=https://issuu.com/gtalumni/docs/1991_66_4 |journal=Georgia Tech Alumni Magazine |volume=66 |issue=4 |pages=44–45}}</ref> Chou received a two-year fellowship from the [[Alfred P. Sloan Foundation]] between 1990 and 1992, as well as a five-year fellowship from the [[David and Lucile Packard Foundation]] (1990–1995).<ref name="iamsas">{{cite news |title=Dr. Mei-Yin Chou (Advanced Materials and Surface Science) |url=https://www.iams.sinica.edu.tw/en/?link=member&id=40&type=def |accessdate=7 January 2019 |publisher=Institute of Atomic and Molecular Sciences, Academia Sinica}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Mei-Yin Chou |url=https://www.packard.org/what-we-fund/science/packard-fellowships-for-science-and-engineering/fellowship-directory/chou-mei-yin/ |accessdate=7 January 2019 |publisher=David and Lucile Packard Foundation}}</ref>

Chou became an associate professor at Georgia Tech in 1993, and was promoted to full professor in 1998.<ref name="vpasmychou">{{cite news |title=Vice President Mei-Yin Chou |url=https://www.sinica.edu.tw/en/articles/16 |accessdate=7 January 2019 |publisher=Academia Sinica |date=26 October 2016}}</ref> Chou held the Advance Professorship in Science from 2002 to 2006, and chaired the physics department between 2005 and 2010.<ref>{{cite news |title=Mei-Yin Chou |url=https://www.iams.sinica.edu.tw/mobile/show_member.php?lang=en&id=40 |accessdate=7 January 2019 |publisher=Institute of Atomic and Molecular Science, Academia Sinica}}</ref> She returned to Taiwan to assume the directorship of the Institute of Atomic and Molecular Sciences at Academia Sinica, and took a joint adjunct professorship at [[National Taiwan University]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Mei-Yin Chou |url=https://www.phys.ntu.edu.tw/webeng/member/main1.aspx?mem_id=178 |accessdate=7 January 2019 |publisher=National Taiwan University}}</ref>

In 2013, Chou was awarded the Outstanding Award of the [[Taiwan Outstanding Women in Science Awards]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.epochtimes.com/b5/13/3/2/n3812794.htm |title=周美吟王素蘭 獲台灣傑出女科學家 |author=陳至中 |publisher=[[The Epoch Times]] |access-date=2026-04-10 |date=2013-03-02 |language=zh-tw}}</ref>

She was elected a fellow of the [[American Physical Society]] in 2002, and elected to membership within Academia Sinica in 2014.<ref name="iamsas"/> Chou was considered one of three finalists for the position of president of [[Academia Sinica]] in 2016.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Chen |first1=Wei-han |title=Wong Chi-huey to leave, as Ma U-turns |url=https://www.taipeitimes.com/News/front/archives/2016/05/11/2003645982 |accessdate=7 January 2019 |work=Taipei Times |date=11 May 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Hsu |first1=Stacy |title=Tsai Ing-wen to appoint new head of Academia Sinica |url=https://www.taipeitimes.com/News/front/archives/2016/05/18/2003646515 |accessdate=7 January 2019 |work=Taipei Times |date=18 May 2016}}</ref> After [[Kuo Way]] withdrew from consideration and [[James C. Liao]] was selected,<ref>{{cite news |last1=Chen |first1=Wei-han |title=Kuo Way turns down Ma interview |url=https://www.taipeitimes.com/News/taiwan/archives/2016/05/17/2003646463 |accessdate=7 January 2019 |work=Taipei Times |date=17 May 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last1=Chung|first1=Jake|title=Liao named Academia Sinica head|url=https://www.taipeitimes.com/News/taiwan/archives/2016/06/04/2003647855|accessdate=7 January 2018|work=Taipei Times|date=4 June 2016}}</ref> Chou was appointed one of three vice presidents.<ref name="vpasmychou"/> In late 2017, Chou was one of eight finalists considered for the position of National Taiwan University president.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Lin |first1=Chia-nan |title=Academia Sinica denies swaying NTU president's selection |url=https://www.taipeitimes.com/News/taiwan/archives/2017/11/21/2003682658 |accessdate=7 January 2019 |work=Taipei Times |date=21 November 2017}}</ref> Chou remained in the running until the final round of five candidates.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Maxon |first1=Ann |title=Ministry offers fix for NTU election woes |url=https://www.taipeitimes.com/News/front/archives/2018/09/13/2003700318 |accessdate=7 January 2019 |work=Taipei Times |date=13 September 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Maxon |first1=Ann |title=NTU academic wants total repeat of vote |url=https://www.taipeitimes.com/News/taiwan/archives/2018/09/26/2003701178 |accessdate=7 January 2019 |work=Taipei Times |date=26 September 2018}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Chou is married to Ye-Hwa Evan Chen.<ref name=":0" /> They have a son and a daughter; her son earned a master's degree from the [[University of Washington]] and her daughter graduated from [[Harvard University]] with a degree in mathematics.<ref name=":1" />
